test_list.description: a/b, http://x and /usr/bin never start a completion token; a slash only counts at byte 0.
$ and @ start a token at the beginning, after whitespace, ( or [ and nowhere else (a$b, dev@x.com).
Text inside backtick spans is never a token.
A cursor inside a multi-byte char or past the end yields no token and no panic.
The description tables cover exactly the names of the two directive tables: no missing, no extra, no duplicates.
Basename prefix ranks above path prefix, above substring, above fuzzy subsequence.
A path with whitespace is inserted as @"path with spaces"; others stay bare.
Even with 1000 matching paths at most 100 suggestions are returned.
Equal-ranked candidates are ordered by byte-wise lexicographic order, independent of index order.
A suggestion's range covers the whole token including text after the cursor.
StaticPathIndex honours the limit and only returns matching paths.
For arbitrary query text and index size the result length is at most 100.
For arbitrary UTF-8 and cursor, detect_token never panics and returned offsets are char boundaries.
